title: Review: feat(jmap-client): implement RFC 8620 base client crate
notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — The codebase is well-structured and the correctness issues found are mostly edge cases (schemeless URL validation, bare id: SSE line, transport-error stream continuation) rather than data-loss or security holes. The two highest-impact items are: (1) Session.state staleness detection is entirely absent, which is a protocol compliance gap that will cause callers to miss server-side session changes silently; and (2) expand_url_template silently leaves unrecognized placeholders in the URL, which produces confusing 404s with no diagnostic. The S1 items (ClientError not non_exhaustive, ClientConfig invariant bypassable via Clone, SseFrame not Clone) are manageable pre-1.0 but will generate issues if the crate is published. The sha256 field in BlobUploadResponse coupling the public API to a draft spec is the most likely source of future breaking-change churn.
Confidence: 25% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: (1) validate_session_urls string-split URL scheme check (JMAP-7xt.1) — the specific attack vector (bare 'https' word passing the check) was identified, but there may be other URL shapes the ad-hoc parser misclassifies that url::Url::parse would catch; (2) subscribe_events unfold loop (JMAP-7xt.3) — the transport-error state=Some path was flagged, but the full state machine has several interacting transitions (raw_buf, scan_from, buf) that were reasoned about statically, not exercised. Uncertainty driven by: (a) no integration tests visible — only unit tests covering parsing; the streaming loop cannot be end-to-end tested without a mock HTTP server, so runtime behavior of the unfold closure under error injection is not verified; (b) blob.rs not read (expand_url_template, upload_blob, download_blob) — the two-stage size cap analysis was based on fetch_session and call; if blob paths differ, there may be missing caps; (c) push/mod.rs StateChange definition not read — assumed correct based on how it is used. Would raise confidence if: integration tests with a mock SSE/WS server were added; blob.rs was read to verify size caps; a fuzzer ran against parse_sse_block and parse_ws_frame.
Idiom rating: NEEDS-WORK — The codebase is structurally sound (blanket impls, Arc for Clone, #[non_exhaustive] on some types, test oracle comments) but has a cluster of related issues: ClientError missing #[non_exhaustive] and exposing two third-party error types (reqwest, tungstenite) in its public interface; JmapClient and WsSession both missing Debug; SseFrame/SseEvent/StateChange/WsFrame missing PartialEq and Clone; one production expect() in send_request that should be a ? return; and #[forbid(unsafe_code)] absent at the crate root. These are P1 API issues that would need fixing before stabilizing the 0.1 semver.
Rust idiom confidence: 85% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: (1) whether AuthProvider::auth_header lifetime change from owned to borrowed is actually feasible given the dyn trait + Arc<dyn AuthProvider> pattern — object-safe lifetime bounds on trait methods require care; (2) whether JmapResponse in jmap-types derives PartialEq (if not, WsFrame cannot derive it either — not checked); (3) the download/upload/event_source URL template fields being String is intentional and correct, so the URL-type issue only applies to api_url. Uncertainty driven by: not reading Cargo.toml dependency versions, not checking jmap-types wire.rs for JmapResponse derives, and not running clippy to catch any remaining annotations.
